excerpt: Macro Defect Inspection. Chip manufacturers deploy advanced macro defect inspection throughout the production line to monitor key process steps, gather process-enhancing information and ultimately, lower manufacturing costs. Field-established tools such as the F30™, NSX®, Firefly®, and the latest Dragonfly® G3 inspection systems are found in the wafer fab (front-end) and packaging (back-end) facilities around the world. These high-speed tools incorporate features such as wafer-less recipe creation, tool-to-tool correlation and multiple inspection resolutions.
scope_note: COMPARATOR ROW, weaker claim than the Firefly/JetStep links above: the source only states that Dragonfly G3 (and F30, NSX, Firefly) macro-inspection systems 'are found in the wafer fab (front-end) and packaging (back-end) facilities around the world' -- i.e. deployed in packaging facilities generically, not 'engineered for' or 'designed for' advanced packaging specifically, and not HBM-specific. Filed as process_relevance rather than supplier_capability for that reason. Dual front-end/back-end deployment, not packaging-exclusive.
notes: W13 RECORDS REVIEW (accept) by claude_w13_records_verifier: Confirmed against onto_10k_fy2025 p.1: the shared Dragonfly/F30/NSX/Firefly sentence states these tools 'are found in the wafer fab (front-end) and packaging (back-end) facilities around the world' -- dual-use placement language, not 'designed for' or 'engineered for' packaging specifically. link_kind process_relevance is correctly the WEAKEST tier here, deliberately weaker than the Firefly/JetStep supplier_capability links above, and the scope_note is explicit about why. This is good, careful differential tiering within a single source passage shared across multiple platforms.

No dollar figure or unit count is given for the inspection/advanced-packaging slice itself -- only the qualitative direction and the $2.6 million NET change for the whole 'systems and software' revenue line (which also includes the offsetting metrology/Advanced-Nodes/SiC increases). Filed at the inspection PARENT category (not multi_equipment) because the sentence specifically names 'our inspection product line', distinct from the metrology product line named in the same sentence. This is Onto's closest approach anywhere in either filing to a quantified advanced-packaging revenue signal, and it is directional only, not a dollar split -- see ONTO-HBM-CONCLUSION in the coverage notes.
